Interesting — it says "arrived next to the target" at (2,7) after 0 legs. So (2,7) IS adjacent to (3,7). That means I'm at (2,7) and (3,7) is the player. So I'm correctly at (2,7). But I can't move to (2,8) or (3,7).

Wait, "arrived next to target" with 0 legs means I'm already adjacent — so the pathfinder thinks I'm fine. But I can't actually step. 

Let me reconsider: maybe the notice board is a solid at (2,7) and I'm standing on it, and the game's collision prevents leaving because... no, that doesn't make sense.

Let me try walking to a tile far away and watch the legs — earlier it did 14 legs but stayed at (2,7). That means each leg tried to move but got blocked. So every adjacent tile is blocked from my position. But the map shows them as '.'. 

Unless... the map legend '@' means I'm there but the actual tile is the notice board (solid), and all 4 neighbors are also somehow blocked. Let me check: is there possibly a wall I'm misreading? Row 7: `#.@P....#` — x0='#', x1='.', x2='@', x3='P', x4-7='.', x8='#'. So (1,7) is '.', (2,8) is '.'. 

Let me try moving to (1,7) — left.
